description:
Aftercare is such a deeply personal thing with so many variables that it’s almost impossible to say exactly how to do aftercare for Locktober specifically. It is such an individual experience. However, I’m going to attempt to give a brief and broad overview of it with some suggestions on things you can do to care for yourself during Locktober.

Sometimes during or after play, people experience something called drop. If you’re new to kink, both aftercare and drop are things I highly recommend researching and learning about.

They’re both things that are relevant to people on either side of the slash. Tops and Dominants can experience drop and need aftercare too, so regardless of whether you’re a giver or a receiver, this is relevant to you.

The TL;DR is:

Drop can happen straight after a scene, a few hours later, or sometimes even the next day. You might feel sad, flat, tired, needy, emotional, irritable, or just a little bit weird and not really know why.

And sometimes you won’t experience it at all. I usually don’t, and it was only when I tried needle play for the first time that I did, and it hit me very hard. Luckily, I knew what to do to take care of myself.

Aftercare is basically the care that happens during or after play to help you come back down to reality, recover, and look after yourself after whatever you’ve just been doing.

Usually, it’s something that’s discussed and negotiated prior to a scene. Some people don’t want aftercare, some people prefer to do it alone, some people love caring for others after a scene, etc. It’s an endless list of possibilities because everyone is so unique, just as every experience is unique.

– Have you slept?

– Are you hydrated?

– Have you moved your body?
